source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Fuel, p.6M-5

procedures.title: Carburetor inlet fuel filter: service
steps: Do not try to clean filter elements; replace a plugged element, and replace it if flooding occurs.
Fit the spring and then the element in the carburetor; a bronze element goes in with the small end of the cone facing out.
Put a new gasket on the inlet fitting nut, screw the nut into the carburetor and tighten securely.
Reconnect the fuel line and tighten the connector.

specs.value: every 12 months or 12,000 miles, whichever first

notes: A plugged filter causes power loss or a rough, pulsing feel, mostly at high engine speed.

procedures.title: Choke coil (V8): replace
steps: Take off the air cleaner and unclip the upper end of the choke rod.

Rochester 4MV and Holley: pry the choke coil shield off with a screwdriver in its cutout and lift it carefully over the rod, then remove the choke rod, bracket screw and choke coil assembly (see figure 7C in the manual).
Install the new choke coil assembly with its locating tab in the forward hole in the intake manifold, and fit the mounting screw.
